args.Message: --- **I TESTS FOR HIP PATHOLOGY** --- **1 HIP SCOUR TEST** PURPOSE To assess for intraarticular hip pathology PROCEDURE • Patient lies supine • Flex the hip and knee • Apply a gentle axial load through the femur • Move the hip through flexion/extension and abduction/adduction while maintaining compression POSITIVE SIGN • Pain • Catching • Clicking • Crepitus • Restricted/abnormal movement INDICATES Possible intraarticular hip pathology such as degenerative or labral pathology --- **2 LEG ROLL TEST** PURPOSE To assess for intraarticular hip pathology and restriction of passive hip rotation PROCEDURE • Patient lies supine with the leg relaxed • Examiner gently rolls the leg from side to side producing internal and external rotation of the hip • Compare with the opposite side POSITIVE SIGN • Pain • Markedly increased or decreased hip rotation • Excessive external rotation compared with the opposite side INDICATES Possible hip joint pathology --- **II TEST FOR LABRAL LESION** --- **4 ANTERIOR LABRAL TEAR TEST** PURPOSE To assess for an acetabular labral lesion particularly an anterior labral lesion PROCEDURE • Patient lies supine • Flex the hip and bring it through the provocative combination of hip movement used to stress the anterior labrum • Reproduce the patients familiar symptoms • Compare with the opposite side POSITIVE SIGN • Reproduction of anterior hip/groin pain • Clicking catching or givingway sensation may occur INDICATES Possible acetabular labral lesion --- **III PEDIATRIC HIP PATHOLOGY** --- **5 BARLOWS TEST** PURPOSE To determine whether an infants hip is unstable and can be dislocated PROCEDURE • Infant lies supine • Flex the hip and knee • Stabilize the pelvis • Gently adduct the hip • Apply gentle posteriorly directed pressure through the femur POSITIVE SIGN • A palpable clunk as the femoral head dislocates INDICATES Dislocatable/unstable hip suggestive of developmental dysplasia of the hip DDH --- **6 GALEAZZI SIGN** PURPOSE To detect apparent femoral shortening particularly due to hip dislocation PROCEDURE • Infant lies supine • Flex both hips and knees to approximately 90 • Place the feet together • Compare the height of both knees POSITIVE SIGN • One knee is lower than the other INDICATES • Developmental hip dislocation/dysplasia • Femoral shortening • Other limblength discrepancy --- **7 ORTOLANI SIGN** PURPOSE To detect a dislocated hip that can be reduced PROCEDURE • Infant lies supine with hips and knees flexed • Stabilize the pelvis • Gently abduct the hip while applying pressure over the greater trochanter in an appropriate direction to reduce the femoral head POSITIVE SIGN • A palpable clunk as the femoral head reduces into the acetabulum INDICATES Reducible hip dislocation DDH Barlow vs Ortolani Barlow OUT dislocates Ortolani IN reduces --- **IV TESTS FOR MUSCLE DYSFUNCTION** --- **8 HIP LAG SIGN** PURPOSE To assess hip extensor muscle function particularly the ability to actively maintain hip extension PROCEDURE • Patient lies prone • Examiner passively extends the hip • Ask the patient to maintain the hip in the extended position after the examiner releases support POSITIVE SIGN • The patient cannot maintain the extended position • The hip falls back toward flexion INDICATES Hip extensor weakness/dysfunction --- **10 THOMAS TEST** PURPOSE To assess hip flexor tightness/hip flexion contracture PROCEDURE • Patient lies supine near the edge of the table • Patient flexes one hip and knee toward the chest to flatten the lumbar spine • Observe the position of the opposite leg POSITIVE SIGN • Opposite thigh rises from the table hip flexor tightness • Knee extends possible rectus femoris tightness • Hip abducts possible TFL/ITB tightness INDICATES Hip flexor muscle tightness/contracture --- **V TESTS FOR HIP DISPLACEMENT** --- **11 NELATONS LINE** PURPOSE To assess the position of the greater trochanter in relation to the pelvis PROCEDURE • Patient lies in the appropriate position with the hip examined • Draw an imaginary line from the ASIS to the ischial tuberosity • Assess the position of the greater trochanter relative to this line POSITIVE FINDING • Greater trochanter lies above Nelatons line INDICATES Possible superior displacement of the femur/hip dislocation --- **12 BRYANTS TRIANGLE** PURPOSE To detect proximal displacement of the greater trochanter and apparent shortening of the femur PROCEDURE • Patient lies supine • From the ASIS draw a perpendicular line to the bed • Draw a line from the greater trochanter to meet this perpendicular • Compare the triangles on both sides POSITIVE FINDING • Shortening of the base of Bryants triangle on the affected side INDICATES Possible hip dislocation or proximal displacement of the femur --- **VI SACROILIAC JOINT TESTS** --- **14 GAENSLENS TEST** PURPOSE To assess SI joint pathology PROCEDURE • Patient lies near the edge of the table • One hip is flexed toward the chest • The opposite leg hangs over the edge • Apply gentle pressure to produce opposite pelvic movements POSITIVE SIGN • Reproduction of pain around the SI joint INDICATES Sacroiliac joint dysfunction/pathology --- **VII OTHER MUSCLE DYSFUNCTION TESTS** --- **17 TRIPOD SIGN** PURPOSE To assess hamstring tightness PROCEDURE • Patient sits with the legs extended • Examiner observes the patients sitting posture • Patient attempts to sit upright POSITIVE SIGN • Patient leans backward and supports themselves with their hands • Knee flexion may occur because of hamstring tightness INDICATES Hamstring tightness/shortness
